statement: Maria Demko was born between 1888 and 1912.
basis: Her grandson (Ahn 2) was born in the early 1960s per the Duska ledger. Two generations of 22 to 35 years each put her birth in this window.
test: Her age in any marriage, census, passenger or death record.

statement: Maria Demko was baptised Greek Catholic.
basis: DM-PR-3 (Rusyn lean), DM-PR-1 (Uzhhorod was the seat of the Mukachevo Greek Catholic eparchy) and DM-L-002 (Iňačovce was a Greek Catholic parish).
test: Denomination column in her baptism, her marriage entry, or her children's baptisms.

history.why: DM-S-001-1 shows a Demko household split by rite: father Greek Catholic, mother Roman Catholic. If Maria is a daughter of that couple (DM-H-009), the usual rule of the period would have her baptised in her mother's church.

statement: The Demkos are the Iňačovce (Solymos) side of the family: Maria was born there and married into a Duska household in Senné.
basis: DM-PR-2 names two villages 4 km apart, and the Duska agent's H-004 places the Duska male line in Senné. The alternative readings (Demko from Senné, or from a third village) are each plausible.
test: Bride's residence and house number in the Duska-Demko marriage entry.

history.why: The only Demko household documented so far is at Viszoka (Vysoká nad Uhom) no. 132, a third village not named in the priors.

statement: Maria Demko was born in a village that is now in Slovakia, not in Ukraine.
basis: Both named villages are on the Slovak side. Against it: a birth record held in Uzhhorod is what one would expect for a village now in Zakarpattia, and Ung county straddled the present border.
test: Birthplace as written in the marriage entry or in any census sheet.

history.why: Viszoka is on the Slovak side of the present border. Only counts if the Viszoka household is hers.

statement: The Uzhhorod record is a Greek Catholic register or register duplicate of the Mukachevo eparchy, and not a civil register.
basis: DM-L-003 catalogues exactly such a series for the Ung district. DM-L-001 shows the Iňačovce Greek Catholic books held at Prešov stop at 1898, which would leave a later baptism outside the Slovak holdings.
test: Whatever told Kevin the record is in Uzhhorod: an archive reply, a catalogue entry, or a fond and file number.

history.why: A Roman Catholic baptism for Maria (possible under DM-H-009) would not be in a Mukachevo eparchy book.

statement: If Maria was born after 1 October 1895, a second, civil birth registration exists for her that does not depend on the Uzhhorod church book.
basis: From training, not yet checked against a source: Hungary introduced state civil registration on that date, kept separately from the churches.
test: Confirm the start date and the present custodian of Ung county civil registers for the birth village, then search the birth year.

statement: Mihaly Duska and Maria Demko married in the old country between 1908 and 1935, and the entry names her father.
basis: DM-H-001 window plus a usual bride's age of 17 to 25. Parish and civil marriage entries of the period normally name both fathers.
test: Marriage entry in the Senné Roman Catholic book (DM-L-007), the Iňačovce books (DM-L-001), or the civil register.

statement: Neither the surname nor a Greek Catholic baptism will be enough to settle whether the Demkos were Rusyn. It will need a language or nationality column.
basis: DM-L-004: Demko occurs as a Polish, Slovak and Ukrainian/Rusyn surname. From training: many Greek Catholics of the Ung lowlands were recorded as Slovak-speaking.
test: Mother-tongue and nationality columns in the 1869, 1900, 1910, 1921 or 1930 census sheets for the Demko household.

history.why: One household, two rites (DM-S-001-1). Denomination was crossing family lines by 1882, so it is a poor proxy for origin.

statement: György Demkó and Mária Hreskó of Viszoka no. 132 are Maria Demko's parents (Ahn 18 and 19). The Mihály baptised in 1882 is her brother.
basis: Same surname in the same county. The collector filed the image under Demko leads and labelled it by the parents' names. Maria shares her given name with the mother. Against: no document links the two, and Viszoka is not one of the villages in DM-PR-2.
test: A baptism of a Mária to this couple at Viszoka 132, or a marriage entry naming Maria's father as György and her home as Viszoka.

statement: The Mihály Demkó baptised in 1882 is Maria Demko's father (Ahn 18). György Demkó and Mária Hreskó are then Ahn 36 and 37.
basis: Competes with DM-H-009. Needs Maria born after about 1902, which is inside the DM-H-001 window. Nothing in the entry favours this reading over the sibling one.
test: Maria's age at marriage or death, and her father's name in her marriage entry.

statement: The strip is cut from a Greek Catholic baptism register: the boy followed his father's rite, and 'Cicarovce' in the file name is the parish seat or the collector's label, not his birthplace.
basis: From training, not yet checked against a source: Hungarian law of 1868 had children of mixed marriages follow the parent of the same sex. The priest's name may read Csurgovich, a surname I associate with Greek Catholic clergy; the reading is uncertain. Against: both godparents and the mother are Roman Catholic, and the strip shows no page header.
test: The full page with its printed header, and the film or DGS number of the image.
